thread:
Ava (Support): Hey @James (Acme) — following up here. You reported a bunch of failed index writes and a spike in API 422s after yesterday's model swap. Can you drop the request id & sample payload you saw?

James (Acme): saw it around 2026-03-14T21:12Z. request_id=rcq-91f2, error: \"indexer rejected vector: dimension mismatch (expected 1536 got 768)\". Sending one sample payload below.

James (Acme): {
  "id": "doc-1123",
  "embedding": [0.003, 0.21, ... (768 floats) ...],
  "metadata": {"user": "acme-beta"}
}

Ava (Support): thanks. That lines up with what we saw in logs. @indexer-bot fired on the backfill job last night with many failures.

indexer-bot: backfill-job-5893 FAILED; first_error="dim mismatch: expected 1536, got 768"; failed_count=4123; last_attempt=2026-03-14T23:07:02Z

Priya (Infra): Quick status dump: Dedicated cluster for acme has mixed model variants on prod: some inference nodes still on text-embed-legacy-1536, some were auto-upgraded to text-embed-lite-768 during canary. Routing rule was supposed to pin by model tag but a stale config allowed both.

Diego (ML): the model swap happened because we pushed a new lightweight variant (for cost savings). We forgot to update the embedding schema contract for that customer. The embedded vector length changed from 1536->768. That explains rejections.

Marcus (Eng): This is tricky because customer has vectors in DB at 1536; new writes at 768 are being rejected by the vector DB (schema validation). We need a short-term mitigation to keep customer app online and a robust backfill plan.

Ava (Support): immediate ask from Acme: 1) Stop 422s so their app doesn't degrade, 2) get backfill going without double-charging them for tokens. They also flagged billing anomalies — they were billed for the failed backfill runs.

Priya (Infra): Immediate mitigation: revert routing for acme to pin to text-embed-legacy-1536. I can flip traffic in ~8 minutes. That will stop new 768-length vectors.

Diego (ML): Agreed revert. Also let's disable new backfill job submissions until we agree on a migration. Can we patch the indexer to accept both dims temporarily and route 768 -> transform?

Marcus (Eng): We can accept both dims by adding an adapter that pads/truncates at write time, but that has correctness implications. Options:
- pad 768 -> 1536 by zero-padding (fast, cheap, may affect similarity slightly)
- project 768 -> 1536 with a learned linear up-project (better quality, requires model infra)
- reject 768 and force customer to re-index from original content (not acceptable)

Ava (Support): Customer prefers automatic migration with minimal manual work. Padding sounds okay for many customers if we document it.

Diego (ML): For immediate unblock do zero-pad to 1536 for writes coming from the new model. We'll flag those vectors as "padded" in metadata so future evaluation can consider them. Longer term, a projection matrix trained offline is better but needs time.

Marcus (Eng): Plan:
1) Priya reverts routing to legacy 1536 (stop new failures).
2) We deploy an indexer-hotfix that accepts 768 vectors and pads to 1536 on ingest; tag = "padded_by_pad-v1". Hotfix + feature-flag to enable only for acme.
3) Re-run backfill job with throttling and idempotency; skip already-succeeded docs.
4) Refund billing for failed backfill attempts and apply a 1-week credit.

Priya (Infra): I reverted routing @ 2026-03-15T00:05Z. Confirmed all inference nodes for acme on text-embed-legacy-1536. No more 768 writes observed in the last 3m.

indexer-bot: backfill-job-5893 paused by operator at 2026-03-15T00:07Z

Marcus (Eng): I'm pushing a small indexer patch to accept dims {768,1536} and pad 768->1536. Feature-flag default off. I'll enable it only for acme. Deployment in ~20m.

Diego (ML): FYI reproducible dev steps for local repro:
1) start local indexer with schema set to 1536.
2) send embedding from text-embed-lite (768) with header X-Client: acme-swap
3) server returns 422 unless adapter enabled.

Logs attached (snippet):
```
ERROR indexer write failed id=doc-1123 err=\"dim mismatch: expected 1536 got 768\" src=request-handler.go:213
WARN routing: node returned model=text-embed-lite-768 for tenant=acme (config pin missing)
```

Ava (Support): Billing note - James says they were charged for backfill-job-5893 attempts. @Marcus can you tag failed job runs and hand over to billing ops for reversal?

Marcus (Eng): Yup. I'll mark the failed runs as system-failed and provide a CSV of request_ids + token_count to billing. Also adding a non-bill flag for retry runs created by our backfill re-run.

James (Acme): Appreciate the quick triage. Any ETA on backfill completion? They estimated ~14M docs.

Priya (Infra): After patch & canary iters, we'll re-run backfill with concurrency 8 and rate-limit 200 writes/sec to avoid DB overload. Rough calc: 14M / (200/sec) ~= 19.4 hours sustained. With parallelism we can target ~8-10 hrs. I'll schedule during low-traffic window (02:00-12:00 UTC).

Diego (ML): Quality check: We'll run spot-queries vs a holdout set to compare retrieval AUC before/after padding. If padding regresses beyond threshold, we block and escalate to ml-research.

Marcus (Eng): Hotfix deployed to canary for tenant=acme at 2026-03-15T00:30Z. Observed acceptance of 768 vectors and write success: id=doc-1123 padded=true

indexer-bot: backfill-job-5893 resumed (canary run) run_id=5893.canary at 2026-03-15T00:45Z; canary_sample=500; failed=0; succeeded=500

Ava (Support): Can we automate a message to the customer's SSO admins so they know we paused/resumed? I'll send a turnaround summary after the canary is green.

James (Acme): can you also confirm token billing adjustments? We got charged for ~4k failed writes and it shows up as ~12k token units on our bill. That's wrong if those were failed.

Marcus (Eng): I'll attach the fail CSV to billing ticket BG-742 and cc you @James. We'll request full reversal for failed attempts and mark retries as non-billable.

Priya (Infra): Postmortem action items so we don't repeat:
- make model->schema contract explicit in routing rules (pin by embed-dim tag)
- add pre-ingest schema validation with soft-fail + telemetry to detect canary leaks
- block auto-upgrade of inference fleet for tenants with pinned schema until explicit ok

Diego (ML): add to that: publish a compatibility matrix for embedding models (dims, version, padding/projection support).

Ava (Support): Next steps for now:
- keep canary running for 6k samples, run quality checks (Diego)
- if pass, schedule full backfill window (Priya)
- billing team to refund failed attempts (Marcus)
- I will send the customer summary and ask to confirm they are OK with padding approach for now.

James (Acme): Sounds good. Please make sure we get a confirmed rollback plan if retrieval quality drops.

Marcus (Eng): noted. I posted the rollback checklist in the incident board and will watch metrics.

Ava (Support): I'll close the immediate customer-facing loop once billing confirms refund and canary passes. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

indexer-bot: backfill-job-5893.canary completed 6k samples at 2026-03-15T02:10Z; failed=0; succeeded=6000; padded_count=6000

Diego (ML): Quick QC results (spot): recall@10 drop = 0.7% (within threshold). Marking canary good.

Priya (Infra): Scheduling full backfill at 2026-03-15T03:00Z with concurrency caps and operator watch.

Ava (Support): Closing loop with customer now. James pls watch for the billing ticket and confirm when refund posts.

James (Acme): Will do, thanks for the fast response.
